messages:
alex-m: Quick sync — planning rollout for tiered latency SLOs (per-tenant). Want a safe canary + feature-flag matrix + fallback policy. My initial thought: pilot with 2–3 enterprise customers, then widen by quota tier. Open to scope negotiation — low-risk first.
sam-chen: +1 on enterprise-only pilot first. Public rollout risks too many variables. Proposed launch criteria: p95 latency delta <= 20ms vs baseline, errors < 0.01, and cost delta < 10% over 48h for pilot tenants. If any fail -> rollback.
priya-r: Implementation notes: feature flags at routing layer so fallback happens before compute. Default fallback = route to `standard` model variant + enable prefix cache. Example flag config we can use in router (pseudo):

```json
{
  "flag": "enable_tiered_sla_v1",
  "scopes": ["tenant_id", "quota_tier"],
  "variants": ["slo_fast", "standard"],
  "rollout": {"pilot": ["tenant-123","tenant-789"]}
}
```

Also add a per-tenant kill switch.
jordan-s: Auto-rollback rules I'd add to infra: if p95(latency) > target for >5min AND request_rate > 10rps, then cut 50% of traffic to `standard` variant and fire pager to #eng-oncall. Tag traces with `slo_rollout=true` to filter.
emily-k: From CS: agree on enterprise pilot, but require comms plan + explicit opt-in for customers. Need a template email + support runbook for degraded quality. Also add a way to exempt specific customers from canary routing.
canary-bot: Canary scheduled by @sam-chen for tenants [tenant-123, tenant-789] starting 2026-05-12T09:03Z. Monitoring dashboards: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/slo-rollout (view-only)
sam-chen: For pro tier we should run an A/B quality check (weighted experiment) rather than full switch. Holdback 5% for quality regression detection — compare embedding cosine similarity + human eval samples. Metric: answer_similarity_mean >= 0.98 vs baseline.
alex-m: Good. I'll draft a rollout matrix with slices and kill conditions. High-level slices: pilot-enterprise (1–2 customers), small-pro (5% pro), broad-pro (25% pro), free-canary (10% low-risk requests). Each slice needs its own stop-criteria.
priya-r: I'll add the router hooks today. Plan: feature flag check -> route decision -> add header `x-slo-variant` -> if breached fallback flag flips. Branch: `feat/sla-rollout`.
jordan-s: PromQL example for p95 by tenant to drive rules (adapt as needed):

```promql
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, tenant_id))
```

Then alert rule: `p95 > target AND sum(rate(requests[5m])) by (tenant_id) > 10`
deploy-bot: Canary started for slice "pilot-enterprise" at 2026-05-12T09:03Z. Live metrics streaming to dashboard. :rocket:
sam-chen: Add experiment logging for all responses in pilot: store hashes + small sample of full responses for offline eval. Retention 7 days.
alex-m: Action items: (1) I’ll publish the matrix + launch checklist, (2) @priya-r implement flag+fallback, (3) @jordan-s add auto-rollback SLO rule and alert, (4) @emily-k prepare customer comms and opt-in form. Target: pilot next Tue if all green. :thumbsup:
priya-r: Yep — will post PR link when ready.
jordan-s: Oncall runbook entry done, will add escalation steps.
emily-k: I'll draft email and opt-in doc, sharing w/ legal for the enterprise pilot.
alex-m: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after first 24h of pilot to decide pro tier experiment plan.
